title: Penetrative radiation in CATKE
author: simone-silvestri
matched_lines: This PR adds a penetrative radiation correction to the convecting path of CATKE. In practice the convective velocity scale $w_\bigstar$ should depend on the external bouyancy forcing which, with penetrative radiation, is not constrained only on the surface but penetrates inside the mixed layer. Therefore, we should account for the integral of this forcing within the mixed layer. We also need to compute the convective length scale, which in CATKE is a measure of the mixed layer depth, and in the case of penetrative radiation requires an inversion to compute. Here it is implemented with 3 Newton iterations which (claude) verified is enough for any practical case.

matched_lines: Side note on the extra MPI: Claude's understanding is that a little extra MPI work is unavoidable for correctness in the current implementation of local grids/topologies. One idea I had around that would be to use a new `FullyConnectedOverlapping` topology with increased size in the x-direction for FC and FF locations (i.e., `Nx+1` like bounded, instead of `Nx`) so that MPI rank north halos perfectly fit the interior of their 180°-rotated partner rank. If this is worthwhile we can do that in another PR?   | These new index-tracing tests fill fields with global index values so that each halo cell's value encodes exactly which source cell it came from. We test that every halo cell matches the serial cell across all 4 stagger locations (CC, FC, CF, FF). In some sense this is stricter test than simulations because they can mask wrong halo values if the error is in a dynamically quiescent region. When the index-tracing test fails, it identifies the affected region (e.g. "north halo"), row, column, and whether the error is a wrong-source value or an unwritten cell. This verbose type of english-language output was _very_ helpful for helping Claude fix the halo-filling errors.
